name: Free Energy Principle (FEP)
title: Free Energy Principle (FEP) — Cognitive-layer theoretical reference
description: Curated reference for the Free Energy Principle (Friston 2006, 2010, 2023): a unifying mathematical framework proposing that self-organising systems minimise an upper bound on sensory surprise (variational free energy) to maintain non-equilibrium steady state. Includes core formalism, active-inference extension, Markov-blanket partition, predictive-coding implementation, empirical predictions, criticisms, and bridge to the EFC/CEM model.

originator.name: Karl J. Friston
originator.affiliation: Wellcome Centre for Human Neuroimaging, University College London

key_equation.name: Variational free energy
key_equation.description: Upper bound on negative log-evidence (surprise); minimising F simultaneously approximates the Bayesian posterior (perception) and selects actions that reduce sensory surprise (active inference).

core_concepts: active inference and expected free energy
